_about: The single source of truth for this platform: what it accepts and what we have learned about it. Every skill, job and script that makes or posts videos for it reads this file; put new findings here, not anywhere else. maxSeconds is the platform's limit. A video longer than that never goes out cut: the video build makes a separate version for this platform of at most versionSeconds, with its own hook, payoff and end card (data.versions.<platform>), and the publisher posts it only when that version exists.
notes: Instagram fetches each video from a public link (video_url): the publisher puts a copy on this repository's "instagram-uploads" release and removes it once the Reel is up. Do not go back to sending the file to Meta's upload host (rupload.facebook.com): from 15 to 18 Nov 2026 it answered ProcessingFailedError to 11 of 17 uploads (container status: OIL Error FILE_NOT_FOUND on Meta's side), 9 of those never posted, and Meta has no fix for it. The Drive copy (data.igDriveId) is only the fallback when the link can't be fetched.

The refusals did not depend on the file. Original HyperFrames renders, short ffmpeg cuts and full ffmpeg re-encodes were all refused and all accepted at different times. The earlier '40 s limit' and 'our encoding fails' notes were wrong readings of the same random refusals. The copy is still a plain libx264 re-encode (crf 20, yuv420p, aac 128k, faststart) so the index is at the front of the file for the link.

maxSeconds is 90 until a longer post is tested. A video over it gets its own version of at most versionSeconds, never a truncated copy. That version still goes through the upload host (the publisher has no link for it yet), so expect it to need retries.
The grid and feed show an early frame: the headline must be readable from frame 0.
No private or scheduled posts through the API.

Posting times (IST) were picked 18 Nov 2026 when we went from 3 to 5 posts a day. Our own data was too thin to choose from (13 Reels, 80-135 views each, no pattern by hour), so they follow published India studies: SocialPilot's Reels study (7:30 AM, 3 PM, 7:30 PM IST) and several India guides that put the peak at 7-9 PM IST. 08:00 catches the morning commute, 12:30 lunch, 16:00 the afternoon break, 19:00 and 21:30 the evening peak. Slots are at least 2.5 h apart so one publish run (up to 25 min, started up to 10 min late) never overlaps the next. Re-check against Insights once 50+ Reels are up. Meta allows about 50 API posts a day, so 5 is far inside it.
